page: Microsoft Azure E16-4ds_v6 is an Edsv6-family virtual machine configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 128.0 GB of system memory, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The underlying hardware features an Intel Xeon 8573C x86_64 processor operating at 4.2 GHz, with 2 physical cores and 2 threads per core. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Local storage is provided via a bundled 945 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results indicate a divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. The server demonstrates strong single-core capabilities, achieving a Geekbench single-core score of 2093.0 and a strong text processing score of 2505.0. However, multi-core and memory throughput metrics are comparatively limited. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance is categorized as weak at 3948.96, and the uncached memory read bandwidth of 34.95 GB/sec is also in the lower tier. Similarly, Redis SET operations perform weakly at 5.57 million operations per second, and medium-model LLM text generation is poor at 4.48 tokens per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E16-4ds_v6 offers high memory density relative to its compute allocation, providing 32.0 GB of RAM per core alongside fast local NVMe storage. This resource profile makes it suitable for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel processing, such as relational database hosting, in-memory caching, and moderate web serving. It is less suited for highly parallelized compute tasks, large-scale software compilation, or real-time LLM text generation due to its lower multi-core and memory bandwidth performance.
